baseline_audit.title: Interlacing families select a leaf below the average largest root
baseline_audit.informal: Common interlacing enables deterministic spectral selection.
hypotheses: A finite nonempty rooted family of real-rooted polynomials of equal positive degree with positive leading coefficients; every sibling family is nonempty and has a common interlacing; internal polynomials are sums of their descendants.
baseline_audit.conclusion: Some leaf $f$ satisfies $\maxroot(f)\le\maxroot(f_{\varnothing})$.
baseline_audit.notes: Selection is existential; no efficient root-computation guarantee is asserted.

baseline_audit.title: Mixed characteristic polynomials: expectation identity and root bound
hypotheses: $A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb C^{d\times d}$ are PSD, $d\ge1$, $m\ge0$; $\mu[A](x):=\left.\prod_{i=1}^m(1-\partial_{z_i})\det(xI+\sum_{i=1}^m z_iA_i)\right|_{z=0}$.
baseline_audit.conclusion: $\mu[A]$ is real-rooted; $A_i=\mathbb E v_iv_i^*$ for independent finitely supported vectors gives $\mu[A]=\mathbb E\det(xI-\sum_i v_iv_i^*)$. If $\sum_iA_i=I$ and $\operatorname{Tr}A_i\le\varepsilon$, then $\maxroot\mu[A]\le(1+\sqrt\varepsilon)^2$.

baseline_audit.title: Near doubly stochasticity certifies rank and capacity
hypotheses: $T(X)=\sum_iA_iXA_i^*$ on $M_n(\mathbb C)$, $n\ge1$, and $\operatorname{cap}(T):=\inf_{X\succ0,\det X=1}\det T(X)$.

baseline_audit.conclusion: If $\operatorname{ds}(T)\le\varepsilon\le1/(n+1)$, then $\operatorname{rank}T(X)\ge\operatorname{rank}X$ for every $X\succeq0$ and $(1-\sqrt{n\varepsilon})^n\le\operatorname{cap}(T)\le1$. baseline_audit.title: Permutation polynomials: quantitative norm comparison with free Haar unitaries
hypotheses: $d\ge2$, $N\ge2$; $S_i^N$ are independent uniform $N$-permutations restricted to $\mathbf1_N^\perp$; $u_i$ are free Haar unitaries in the reduced group C*-algebra.

$P\in M_D(\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C\langle u,u^*\rangle$ is self-adjoint of degree $q_0\ge1$; $K:=\sup_{V}\|P(V,V^*)\|$, supremum over all unitary tuples in all dimensions; $0<\varepsilon<K-\|P(u,u^*)\|$.
baseline_audit.conclusion: $\mathbb P\{\|P(S^N,S^{N*})\|\ge\|P(u,u^*)\|+\varepsilon\}\le\frac{CD}{N}(Kq_0\log d/\varepsilon)^8\log(eK/\varepsilon)$, with universal $C$.
baseline_audit.notes: Restriction removes the trivial representation. The full universal norm K differs from the reduced free norm in the event; this is an upper-tail theorem, not a local law.

baseline_audit.title: Finite free additive convolution: matrix identity and root barriers
hypotheses: $p(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ia_ix^{d-i}$ and $q(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ib_ix^{d-i}$ are monic degree-$d$ real-rooted polynomials, $d\ge1$; $p\boxplus_dq:=\sum_{k=0}^d(-1)^kx^{d-k}\sum_{i+j=k}\frac{(d-i)!(d-j)!}{d!(d-k)!}a_ib_j$.
baseline_audit.conclusion: $p\boxplus_dq$ is real-rooted; if $p=\chi_A,q=\chi_B$ for Hermitian $A,B$ and Haar $U\in U(d)$, then $p\boxplus_dq=\mathbb E\chi_{A+UBU^*}$. For $w>0$, $\mathcal R_{p\boxplus_dq}(w)\le\mathcal R_p(w)+\mathcal R_q(w)$, where $\mathcal R_p(w)=K_p(w)-1/w$ and $K_p$ inverts $p'/(dp)$ above the largest root. Equality holds precisely when $p$ or $q$ is $(x-\lambda)^d$.
baseline_audit.notes: Expected characteristic polynomial; no spectral-probability guarantee.

baseline_audit.title: The matrix Dyson solution is a compactly supported matrix Stieltjes transform
hypotheses: $A\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ Hermitian, $N\ge1$; complex-linear $\mathcal S:M_N\to M_N$ preserves PSD matrices and is self-adjoint for $\langle R,T\rangle=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(R^*T)$.
$M:\mathbb H\to M_N(\mathbb C)$ is the holomorphic positive-imaginary solution of $-M(z)^{-1}=zI-A+\mathcal S[M(z)]$.
baseline_audit.conclusion: There is a unique PSD matrix-valued measure $V$ with $V(\mathbb R)=I$, supported on $[-\kappa,\kappa]$, $\kappa=\|A\|_2+2\|\mathcal S\|_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}$, such that $M(z)=\int(\tau-z)^{-1}V(d\tau)$; here the norm of $\mathcal S$ is induced by the matrix spectral norm. Also $\|M(z)\|_2\le1/\operatorname{Im}z$.
